title: docs(security): add public Security FAQ (high-level) aligned to enablement kit v2
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Adds a public-facing Security FAQ (high level) page that mirrors the safe subset of the internal Enterprise Security FAQ v2; aligns terminology/links with the updated enablement kit.
description: Context: Sales/SEs asked for a single public link we can send early in security review cycles (or for partner-led deals) that answers the most common questions without triggering NDA-only evidence sharing. This PR adds a public “Security FAQ (High level)” page derived from the internal Enterprise Security FAQ v2 and the one-pagers pack, with explicit scoping language and shared-responsibility notes across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key goals: (1) keep content safe for public distribution (no SOC 2 report links, no pen test artifacts, no customer-sensitive process details), (2) match enablement-kit terminology and deployment-mode boundaries, (3) ensure all links resolve and point to public-safe destinations, and (4) include a clear “how to request evidence” call-to-action for prospects under NDA. Notes: This is intentionally a subset; it does not cover all FAQ questions (e.g., detailed audit log schemas, remediation SLAs by severity beyond the public SDLC summary, or customer-specific incident timelines).
commits: docs: add Security FAQ (high-level) page (MDX) with hosted/dedicated/private callouts
docs: wire Security FAQ into sidebar + security index and add redirects
docs: link hygiene + terminology alignment (Dedicated vs Private wording, evidence request CTA)
conversation: Elliot Price (author): Added a public Security FAQ page that mirrors the safe subset of the internal Enterprise Security FAQ v2. I tried to keep this strictly “public safe”: no NDA-only evidence, no customer-specific commitments. Would love Security/GRC eyes on the exact phrasing for incident notification + audit logging scope and any places we should soften language. Also, I aligned “Hosted / Dedicated / Private” naming to the enablement kit and updated a couple existing docs pages to match the same phrasing.

Naomi Feldman (reviewer): Overall structure looks good and matches the enablement kit. Two required changes: (1) in the incident notification answer, remove “within 72 hours” and make it contract-dependent / without committing to a specific timeline on the public site; (2) in the retention answer, clarify that default retention varies by deployment mode and configuration, and route detailed retention controls to the dedicated one-pager / contact path rather than implying a single default across all offerings.

Elliot Price (author): Updated incident language to “as required by contract and applicable law” and added “timelines are defined in customer agreements.” Retention answer now explicitly separates Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and avoids stating a single universal default; added a pointer to contact security for mode-specific configuration details.

Marcus Lin (reviewer): Audit logging section: please avoid “all admin actions are logged.” Recommend “Redwood records audit events for key administrative and security-relevant actions in the Console/control plane” and then provide examples. Also please make sure we don’t imply SIEM export is universally available; it’s different across deployment modes.

Elliot Price (author): Adjusted audit logging wording: replaced “all” with “key” and added examples list (API key lifecycle, SSO config changes, role changes, org settings). Added explicit note: export options differ by Hosted/Dedicated/Private and may require enterprise configuration.

Olga Petrov (reviewer): Evidence request CTA: good to include, but keep it generic. Don’t mention NDA process details or turnaround SLAs on the public page. Also, can you add a short disclaimer that third-party reports (SOC 2) are available upon request under NDA, without naming auditors or report periods?

Elliot Price (author): Updated CTA to “Contact security@redwoodinference.com to request compliance evidence (e.g., SOC 2 report) under NDA where applicable.” Removed internal process references and any timing language.

Wei Chen (reviewer): Minor doc style: can we use the same term everywhere (“Redwood Console” not “console”), and standardize “Dedicated” capitalization. Also, the “data residency” answer should link to the public deployment-modes page section that explains data flow differences, not the internal one-pager.

Elliot Price (author): Standardized “Redwood Console” capitalization and “Dedicated” usage; updated the data residency link to the public deployment-modes doc section (and added a short “what changes by mode” table).

Soojin Lee (reviewer): From a GTM perspective this is great. One suggestion: add a single sentence at the top clarifying this is a “high-level overview” and that customers can request the full enterprise kit during security review.
Elliot Price (author): Added top-of-page disclaimer: “This page is a high-level overview; enterprise customers can request additional security documentation during formal security review.”
Naomi Feldman (reviewer): Approved after latest changes. Please ensure the internal enablement kit links remain Confluence/Drive only; public docs should not point to any restricted resources.
Marcus Lin (reviewer): Approved. Thanks for cleaning up the audit logging language.
Olga Petrov (reviewer): Approved. Evidence request phrasing is now public-safe.
content_snippet: New page includes sections: Overview and scope; Deployment modes and shared responsibility (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private); Data handling (customer inputs/outputs, training usage statement, telemetry/logs at a high level); Encryption (in transit/at rest with KMS note); Authentication and access control (SSO/SAML, RBAC, least privilege); Audit logging (examples of events and note on export availability by mode); Vulnerability management and secure SDLC (high-level); Incident response and notification (non-committal, contract-dependent); Compliance evidence request (SOC 2 under NDA where applicable); Contact. Page explicitly avoids: SOC 2 report attachments, pen test summaries, specific remediation SLAs, or customer-specific incident timelines.
notes_for_reviewers: This PR is intended to be the public “safe subset” companion to the Security Enablement Kit v2. Please sanity-check: (1) no over-commitments (“always/never/all”), (2) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private boundaries are accurate, (3) no restricted evidence/process links appear on the public site, (4) language matches the updated enablement kit terminology.
